title: Phawar of Noble Speech (Akor Kren Akor Khana)
cultural_context: Radhon Singh Berry's foundational rhyming rules governing speech, prohibiting slander, deceit, and arrogance, from 'Ka Jingsneng Tymmen'.

khasi: Ka ktien kaba thiang ka pynjem dohnud,
Ka ktien kaba khor ka pynkhih ding;
Wat kren lamwir ha khmat uba bun,
Wat pyniapher ia ki kur ki kha;
Kren beit da ka hok bad ka jingshisha,
Kum u mawkordor ba la pynkhuid;
Uba nang ban bat ia la ka shyntur
Un ioh ka jingsuk ha ka pyrthei.
english: A gentle, sweet word softens the hardest heart,
A venomous word kindles a consuming fire;
Speak not deceitfully before the council of the people,
Sow no discord between maternal and paternal kin;
Speak directly with righteousness and truth,
Like an unblemished jewel purified from dross;
He who knows how to guard his tongue
Shall inherit peace throughout the earth.

khasi: Wat leh khyllah ban kynthoh briew,
Wat buh jingmut basniew ha dohnud;
Ka ktien ba la mih na ka shyntur
Kam ju lah ban phai pat sha ling;
To bthah ia la ka mynsiem baroh,
Ban ri ia ka akor ba kyntang;
Ba ka ktien jong pha kan ai jingim
Sha kito kiba don ha ka jynjar.
english: Commit no foolish fault by slandering others,
Harbor no bitter malice in your breast;
A spoken word that has flown from the lips
Can never be recalled back home;
Admonish your whole soul and mind,
So that your words may impart life and hope
Unto those weighed down by sorrow and distress.
